veil-v2-hovers.detail: Light pressure (0.0174 m/s²) and Venus's gravity both point toward Venus; the shade falls with 0.0347 m/s² and reaches Venus in about 1 d.

veil-hovers.detail: At 1.11 × 10⁶ km sunward of Venus the forces on a Veil with a lightness of 0.0077 balance. The point is unstable along the Sun line, so holding it takes constant trimming, by tilting slats, which the model does not size.

veil-leak-fits.detail: Gaps of 0.05% plus 0.03% through the closed slats, against the 0.1% the closed Veil may let through.

second-law.detail: The pumps reach 50% of the Carnot limit, so the model charges 4.46 × 10²⁷ J of work for 5.3 × 10²⁶ J of heat, more than the 6.2 × 10²⁶ J even a reversible pump would need if every joule left from 737 K.

exhaust-entropy.detail: The model charges pump work as if the hot side were at 1,600 K. Light at 0.37 MW/m² squeezed into a 0.4 µm band around 2.3 µm and a 25° cone counts as at least 9,000 K, 5.6 times hotter. Lifting a joule from the 737 K air into that light takes 9.6 times the work the budget charges.

exhaust-clears-veil.detail: Seen from Venus the Veil is 0.68° in radius. Tiles that face it tilt their 25° cones 13° off the Sun line, which keeps every cone 64° clear of the horizon.

graphite-for-caps.detail: 4.6 × 10¹⁷ kg of graphite by the end of sealing; the caps need 2.5 × 10¹⁷ kg.

ice-arrives.detail: Lowering 1.0 × 10²⁰ kg runs from 30 June 2035 to 15 December 2036, and the Ring can only lower what it has caught. When lowering begins it holds 36% of the ice. The last launch, on 14 April 2035, leaves room for the slowest transfer from Ceres's drifted orbit, 611 d; the last Brick arrives on 15 December 2036, 0 d before lowering ends.

ring-ready-for-ice.detail: The fastest transfer the schedule uses takes 310 d, so Bricks from the first launch on 28 August 2033 can reach Venus on 3 July 2034; the Ring is complete on 31 December 2033.

ceres-ground-heat.detail: All the heat made at Ceres is 110 times what its whole surface could radiate at 1,500 K (8.0 × 10¹⁷ W), so the Crown sheds it in space; the barrels leave 1.1 × 10¹⁷ W on the ground, radiators over 14% of the surface.

ceres-receiver-cooling.detail: At 40 MW/m² each square metre of receiver hands 10 MW/m² to its coolant, against the 10 MW/m² ITER's divertor is built to carry; left to radiate it alone, a receiver would reach 3,100 K.

crown-orbit.detail: The Crown circles at 1,190 km and its fins reach 7,200 km, well inside half of Ceres's 220,000 km Hill radius, where orbits around a small body stay bound; Ceres's recoil, 1.5 × 10⁻⁵ m/s², is small beside its 0.0012 m/s² pull even at the fins' edge.

crown-tethers.detail: Summed from the surface to the Crown, Ceres's net pull on a tether is 59 kJ/kg, against the 3.9 MJ/kg carbon fibre holds at full strength; hanging the 1.4 × 10¹³ kg of cables and holding the beams' 4.8 × 10¹¹ N push takes 3.0 × 10¹¹ kg of fibre.

ceres-ready-in-time.detail: The seed leaves Earth on 1 October 2028, with the Foundry's once Ouroboros-0 has passed, and lands on 16 January 2030; doubling every 45 d, the factories finish the 1.2 × 10¹⁴ kg of Railheads and Crown on 14 July 2033, against a first launch on 28 August 2033.

railheads-within-lattice.detail: Throwing 1.0 × 10²⁰ kg in 1.6 yr takes 1.1 × 10²⁰ W, and until the first Brick is caught on 3 July 2034 only the Lattice's 1.2 × 10²⁰ W can supply it.

ceres-clear-of-jupiter.detail: At its new aphelion Ceres stays 1.64 AU inside Jupiter's closest approach to the Sun, 4.6 of Jupiter's Hill radii against the 2√3 that keeps two orbits from meeting; its Tisserand parameter falls from 3.31 to 3.21, still above the 3 below which Jupiter takes control.

ring-energy-loop.detail: The Ring recovers 2.2 × 10²⁰ W against the 1.1 × 10²⁰ W the Railheads draw.

ring-holds-stator.detail: The 7.0 × 10¹² kg rotor, faster than orbital speed, presses outward enough to carry the 3.0 × 10¹² kg stator with 3.0 × 10¹³ N to spare.

ring-carries-equipment.detail: The receivers, their fins and the catch's radiators weigh 4.8 × 10¹³ kg at the densities the plan uses on Ceres; the rotor's spare lift carries 3.9 × 10¹² kg, 12 times too little.

ring-net-force.detail: Catching half the Bricks eastbound and half westbound cancels the twist, not the force: 6.0 × 10¹⁶ N remains along Venus's orbital motion. An orbital ring has no stiff way to hand an in-plane force to the planet; its spare lift is 3.0 × 10¹³ N, 2,000 times too little.

ring-lowering-load.detail: Lowering 2.2 × 10¹² kg/s needs at least 4.7 × 10¹⁵ N; the rotor's spare lift is 3.0 × 10¹³ N, 150 times too little.

foundry-affords-veil.detail: The Foundry stands still for 9.8 d to build the 5.4 × 10¹¹ kg Veil, whose last parts leave Mercury on 16 September 2032; one doubling is 60 d.

foundry-size.detail: After 27 doublings the 1.3 × 10¹⁴ kg Foundry builds the 8.8 × 10¹³ kg Lattice in 57 d and the Ring in 6.4 d: both done 1683 days after landing, against 1687 with one doubling fewer and 1712 with one more.

foundry-builds-ring.detail: After the Lattice, the Foundry builds the 1.0 × 10¹³ kg Ring in 6.4 d; its last parts reach Venus on 18 November 2033, and the Ring must be complete on 31 December 2033.

aegis-structure.detail: The coil's field pulls on its winding with 1.2 × 10¹¹ N; holding it takes at least 2.0 × 10¹¹ kg of carbon fibre at full strength, 0.13 days of the full Foundry's output against the 60 d of one doubling.

traj-heat-books.detail: The Exhaust lifts 6.1 × 10²⁶ J: Venus's 5.3 × 10²⁶ J, less the 1.6 × 10²¹ J still held by the CO₂ the Frost Towers leave in the air, plus 8.1 × 10²⁵ J that enters while the pumps run. The two sides agree to rounding. This confirms the simulation's own bookkeeping; a heat source the simulation leaves out cannot show here (see the loss-heat check).

frozen-before-sealing.detail: The simulated seas are frozen through on 13 February 2036, leaving 200 d to the last cap on 1 September 2036: the crawler-rafts must lay 750,000 km²/d.

frost-before-sealing.detail: The simulated Frost Towers finish on 9 April 2036; the last caps are sealed on 1 September 2036.

loss-heat-fits.detail: The receivers shed 4.0 × 10¹⁹ W at full power and the catcher tracks 5.4 × 10¹⁹ W, from fins that radiate from both faces: 28% of their light falls on Venus from the Ring, 41% from the canopies. That is 2.7 × 10¹⁹ W with the Lattice at full power and the Ring catching, which the published simulation leaves out. Counting it, the Frost Towers never finish in the simulated years, against the last caps sealed on 1 September 2036.

genesis-by-deadline.detail: Seeding waits for the oxygen (30 September 2036) and for the oceans to hold their pH (1 December 2036), so it begins on 1 December 2036; doubling every 1 d, the cells reach bloom density on 12 December 2036, against a deadline of 31 December 2036.

earth-like-by-deadline.detail: The day-by-day simulation reaches Earth-like conditions on 30 September 2036, 92 d before the 31 December 2036 deadline. The chimneys, not the power, set the pace on 160 d of it.

ozone-model-earth.detail: 280 DU against 279 DU from a three-dimensional model of the pre-industrial Earth, within a quarter either way, with nothing fitted.

ozone-shield-in-time.detail: One day of sunlight makes 49.9 DU, easily measured. The column reaches 185 DU on 2 December 2036, 91 d after the Veil opens, so lichens and mosses go onto land from 2 December 2036, against a deadline of 31 December 2036.

energy-closes.detail: Lattice supply 1.3 × 10²⁸ J against demand 1.1 × 10²⁸ J: 11% spare before the Ring's recovered energy, 32% once the Ring pays for the Railheads.

energy-closes-with-ring.detail: The Lattice delivers 1.3 × 10²⁸ J against 8.6 × 10²⁷ J once the Ring pays for the Railheads, and the Ring recovers 1.1 × 10²⁸ J against the 2.7 × 10²⁷ J of launches it pays for.
